Ltd. vs Union Of India And 3 Others on 1 October, 2019 Author: Prakash Padia Bench: Prakash Padia High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 6 Case :- Writ - C No. - 32527 of 2019 Petitioner :- M/S Tapan Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. Respondent :- Union Of India And 3 Others Counsel for Petitioner :- Neeraj Rai,Prateek Rai
texts.facts: The petitioner has preferred this present writ petition with the prayer to quash the order dated 25.09.2019 passed by Commissioner for Food Safety/Chief Executive Officer/respondent no. 3 by which the appeal preferred by the petitioner under section 32 (4) (a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called as Act '2006') was rejected. the perusal of the record notice dated 06.05.2019 issued against the petitioner. Challenging the aforesaid notice the appeal was preferred by the petitioner before respondent no. 3 as provided under section 32 (4) (c) of Food Safety and Standards act, 2006. The aforesaid appeal preferred by the petitioner before the respondent no. 3 was rejected by him vide order dated 25.09.2019, copy of which is appended as (Annexure-1 to the writ petition). It appears from the perusal of the record that a notice dated 06.05.2019 was issued by the Food Director, Central Licence Authority, (Lucknow and Chandigarh Reason) FSS AI, to the present petitioner. The aforesaid noitce was challenged by the petitioner by filing an appeal as provided under section 32 (4) (a) of the Act of 2006.
texts.arguments: It is argued by Sri Navin Sinha, learned Senior Advocate that the order impugned passed by the respondent no. 3 is absolutely non speaking order. It is further argued that no reasons has been assigned by the respondent no. 3 by passing the order impugned. It is further contended that from M/S Tapan Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. vs Union Of India And 3 Others on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18180455/ 1 Under Section 32 of the Act 2006 it is provided that if the designated officer has reasonable ground for believing that any food business operator has failed to comply with any regualtions to which this section applies, he may issue a notice to the food business operator. It is further provided under Sub Rule 4 that any person who is aggrieved by the notice may appeal to the Commissioner of Food Safety whose decision thereon, shall be final. Section 32 of the Act of 2006 is reproduced below:- 32. Improvement notices. (1) If the Designated Officer has reasonable ground for believing that any food business operator has failed to comply with any regulations to which this section applies, he may, by a notice served on that food business operator (in this Act referred to as an "improvement notice")? (a) state the grounds for believing that the food business operator has failed to comply with the regulations; (b) specify the matters which constitute the food business operator's failure so to comply; (c) specify the measures which, in the opinion of the said Authority, the food business operator must take, in order to secure compliance; and (d) require the food business operator to take those measures, or measures which are at least equivalent to them, within a reasonable period (not being less than fourteen days) as may be specified in the notice. (2) If the food business operator fails to comply with an improvement notice, his licence may be suspended. (3) If the food business operator still fails to comply with the improvement notice, the Designated Officer may, after giving the licensee an opportunity to shows cause, cancel the licence granted to M/S Tapan Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. vs Union Of India And 3 Others on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18180455/ 2 him; Provided that the Designated Officer may suspend any licence forthwith in the interest of public heath for reasons to be recorded in writing. (4) Any person who is aggrieved by- (b) refusal to issue a certificate as to improvement; or (c) cancellation or suspension or revocation of licence under this Act, may appeal to the Commissioner of Food Safety whose decision thereon, shall be final. (5) The period within which such an appeal may be brought shall be ? (a) fifteen days from the date on which notice of the decision was served on the person desiring to appeal; or (b) in the case of an appeal under sub-section (1), the said period or the period specified in the improvement notice, whichever expires earlier; It further appears from the perusal of the record that although statutory appeal was preferred by the petitioner as provided under Sub-section 4 of Section 32 of the Act of 2006, the same was rejected by the respondent no. 3 vide order dated 25.09.2019.
